# Code of Conduct

## Our commitment

Medical Admission Pro is an educational project for students and contributors. We want project spaces to remain respectful, welcoming, safe, and focused on learning and constructive collaboration.

Everyone participating in project spaces is expected to help make participation a positive experience, regardless of age, disability, experience level, education, nationality, race, religion, gender identity, or personal background.

## Expected behaviour

- Use welcoming, respectful, and inclusive language.
- Be patient when explaining technical or educational topics.
- Give and receive constructive feedback gracefully.
- Focus discussion on the problem, evidence, and possible solutions.
- Respect different levels of experience and learning pace.
- Protect other people's privacy and personal information.
- Follow the project's security and responsible-disclosure guidance.

## Unacceptable behaviour

- Harassment, bullying, threats, or discriminatory conduct.
- Personal attacks, insults, intimidation, or repeated hostile comments.
- Sexualized comments or unwanted sexual attention.
- Publishing another person's private information without permission.
- Sharing credentials, private student records, or confidential vulnerability details.
- Spam, impersonation, or deliberately disruptive behaviour.
- Encouraging unsafe or unlawful activity in project spaces.

## Scope

This Code applies to repository Issues, Pull Requests, Discussions (if enabled), Wiki pages, commit messages, and other spaces where someone is representing Medical Admission Pro or its community.

## Reporting and enforcement

Report conduct that violates this Code privately to the project maintainer through the contact method shown on the maintainer's GitHub profile. Do not include unrelated students' private information in a report.

The maintainer will review reports, respect reporter confidentiality as far as reasonably possible, and take proportionate action. Actions may include editing or removing content, requesting a correction, closing a discussion, restricting participation, or blocking an account from project spaces.

Maintainer decisions should be fair, consistent, and focused on keeping the project safe and constructive.
